title: Wouldst Thou in Thy Lonely Hour
description: Wouldst Thou in Thy Lonely Hour in Tonic Solfa to VIENNA, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 92, “Silent Worship”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to VIENNA; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Wouldst thou in thy lone-ly hour Prais-es to th'E-ter-nal pour? I will teach thy soul to be Tem-ple, hymn, and har-mo-ny.

lines: Wouldst thou in thy lonely hour
I will teach thy soul to be
Thou shalt for thine offering bring;
Loves to linger, loves to reign,
In that calm of quiet thought
Wouldst thou in thy lonely hour
Thus thy soul may learn to be

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to VIENNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
